en: Hmm. Good. You're comin' along alright.
Well, ya heard it about a billion times already, so ya oughta know by now. The music for round one is a cutesy pop song, called "So Much More!"
T-Set's specialty is hard dance numbers, so this song takes 'em a little outta their element.
So, first round, I think ya got a chance. But ya better bust your butt practicin' if ya wanna win beyond that.
All right, I will! Thank you very much!
Whaddya know? That wasn't half bad.
If ya can't even do this, then I'm wastin' my time here! Now, focus!
(Should I try a lesson?)
(This is no time to be having a lesson.)
(I might injure myself if I try to do a lesson when I'm so tired.)
(Time is running out, but I'd better rest before I try to do a lesson.)
Ugh, I told you it would sell out. Unbelievable!
Sorry. I had no idea Yoko's book would sell out even at half price.
(Yoko's book? Don't tell me...)
(Has it really sold out? What am I going to do now?)
(Hmm, what about that used bookstore across Iwao Bridge? It's over near the entrance to Bunzaemon Outdoor Mall. Maybe they have it!)
(Okay, time to look for Yoko-san's book.)
Umm, where would it be? Maybe it's in the beauty section...
(I guess I'm out of luck here, too. And there aren't any more bookstores around here, so... I might as well go check in with Yoko-san.)
What the heck was that?
What a complete waste of time.
(I guess that didn't go over too well.)
(But I won't give up. Uncle Kaz taught me better than that! I won't let him down!)
That was great!
You just got yourself a new fan!
Wow, thank you! I hope you'll keep rooting for me!
(I really nailed that performance!)
(I can feel proud telling Yoko-san about this!)
(This is the spot Yoko-san was talking about. But... Am I really going to sing here?)
(What's this piece of paper? Oh, it's a note. Wait, it's from Yoko-san!)
Dear bumpkin, I want you to sing here in front of people who have no idea who you are.
Report back to me if you're able to win the crowd over by the end of your song.
P.S. Make sure you stand on the beer crate when you sing.
Wait, I have to sing on a beer crate? So I can't even dance?
Hm? Are you going to perform or something?
Well, hurry up. I don't have all day.
I can do this. I just have to believe in myself.
So... What did you think?
Still a little rough around the edges, but you've got appeal. I don't think I can even call you bumpkin anymore.
Haha, that's a relief. Thank you so much for all you've done for me, Yoko-san.
Truth be told, I'm a little disappointed. But like they say about parents, it's the worst of the kids you find the cutest.
I'm sorry, Yoko-san. I really wanted my last performance for you to be my best. Still...
I'm never going to forget all you taught me, and I'll treasure this costume you gave me forever.
Keep at it, and one day you'll perform on an even bigger stage in my costume. I can't wait to see you do that... Haruka.
Yes! You finally said my name!
What, do you have a problem with that? Hmph! I take it back! You'll always be a bumpkin to me!
Hehehe, whatever you say, Yoko-san.
Well, I guess I should get going, but I'm so glad I was able to see you in the costume I designed for my friend. He was really special.
What? Did you just say "he," Yoko-san?
That's right. Why wouldn't I? I mean, I was so happy to see you in his costume, so...
What!? Seriously!? You mean that friend you've been talking about wasn't a girl?
Huh? When did I ever say my friend was a girl? Besides, one look at that costume, and anyone could see it was made for a guy!
Umm, it sure looks like a girl's costume to me.
Come on, bumpkin! You have to learn to think outside the box. Get with the times, girl!
Oh, of course...
Yoko-san!
Oh, Uda-san!
(That's right! Uda-san was Yoko-san's boyfriend a long time ago!)
Oh, Uddie...
I'm sorry, Yoko-san! It was all my fault! I should have told you before I quit the idol business. I never knew it hurt you so much.
What? He... He used to be an idol!?
Uddie... Uddie!
Yoko-san! *sniff*
Uddie! Uddie!!!
I have... no idea what's going on.
Oh, you never heard? That kid Yoko-chan wished she could have helped? She was talking about Uda-san.
Whaaaaaat!?
I'm so sorry, Yoko-san! Please forgive me!
No, it was all my fault, Uddie! I promised you we'd make it to the top together, but then I abandoned you!
But... Yoko-san said Uda-san was an old boyfriend!
He was, in a way. They need each other, and they accept each other as they are. In that sense, they're more than lovers.
They might have been lovers too, of course. There's nothing wrong with that, you know. Ah, to be young again. Ugh, I'm so jealous!
Oh, thank you, Momi-chan! It was you who brought Uddie here, wasn't it?
Mhm. I heard you were leaving, and I figured that you two hadn't even met up yet.
But I suppose it's really Haruka-san you should be thanking. She's the one who told me you were leaving.
Thank you, Haruka. I've had that monkey on my back for far too long. I feel absolutely liberated!
Yes. Thank you, Haruka-san.
But to think, you knew Yoko-san all along, Haruka-san. This can't be just a coincidence.
I was surprised, too. I mean, I never would have suspected that you used to be an... um... idol.
Heh, well, that was a long time ago. It was just too competitive for me. Though Yoko-san stayed and kept fighting...
Anyway, I may have failed as an idol, but I always wanted to put smiles on people's faces one way or another.
Putting on those events with you was my way of doing just that.
Uda-san... I had no idea.
I want you to keep spreading your joy on stage! Become the idol I could never be!
That's right. Never forget that you and your costume are simply brimming with Uddie's⑬er, I mean, Uda-san's and my hopes and dreams.
Yoko-san, don't worry! I'll work hard for all three of us!
Good answer. And delivered with just the right enthusiasm, too!
I may be leaving town, but that's no excuse for you to slack off! And don't let me hear you've been causing problems for Uda-san, or else!
Okay! Yoko-san, thank you for all you've done!
I'll see you around, then, bumpkin. I mean... Haruka!
You can now trigger the <Color:7>Climax Heat<Color:Default> state at any time thanks to everything Yoko has taught you.
Whenever you use <Color:7>Climax Heat<Color:Default> from now on, the Climax Heat Gauge won't go down.
(I have to win the crowd over like Yoko-san said.)
(Should I start singing now?)
(Maybe I'll try later.)
(Okay, it's show time! I'm really going to do it this time!)
(Oh, that job didn't go very well at all. I feel so exhausted all of a sudden.)

Well, that just about wraps it up. Hopefully now you have a
good understanding of how the show is going to go.
Yes. Thank you very much.
All right. We're through here, then. Thank you!

(Phew. Okay. That meeting's done. I'd better get back to the
agency.)
Hold it right there! Sawamura-chan?
Um... Yes?
Heheheh, well, aren't you a cute little thing?
Huh? I'm sorry, can I help you with something!?

Oh, that's right. I didn't introduce myself, did I? I'm the
producer on the informational show, "Campus Festival." The
name's Takami.

Oh, the producer? My apologies if I was rude. Yes, I'm
Haruka Sawamura of Dyna Chair.

Sure! I know who you are. I never miss an episode of the
Princess League! I've been rooting for you since the
beginning, you know.
Oh, you have? Thank you very much.

If I may say, you're even cuter in person than you are on
TV.

Absolutely! Yeah, I think you're just great. Say, how'd you
like to be on my show?

Yeah, sure! After all, I have the final word on who gets to
be on the show.
Oh, well, thank you very much!
Heheh. There's just one thing, though.
And I think you know what I mean.
Don't pretend to be so naive. You know the drill, right?

I put you on my show, and you keep me company for a night. A
little business deal.
You're talking about sleeping my way up the ladder!?

Hey, keep your voice down! And don't act so shocked.
Surely you've done something like this at least a time or
two.
I most certainly have not! Let go of me!

C'mon. What have you got to lose? It could be a great
opportunity for you!
Hey, what do you think you're doing!?
Damn. Who asked you to poke your nose in?

Hmph. Forget it, then. I thought this girl would recognize a
good business opportunity when she saw one, but I guess I
was wrong.

Well, good luck with your "career." I think you're going to
find it's harder getting up that ladder than you thought.
Are you all right? Did he hurt you?
I'm fine. He just grabbed my wrist.

That Takami guy is infamous for trying to swoop up young
girls like that. You weren't going to go along with it, were
you?

Good. I'd hate to think our opponent was doing anything like
that to get ahead.
Well, I'd better get going.
Thank you! Thank you for saving me.

Look, I wasn't trying to rescue you or anything. It's just
I hate that crap Takami tries to pull.

He tried the same thing with me once, too. Of course, I
didn't go along with it, either. I just can't stand to see
him up to his old tricks.

Anyway, you'd better watch yourself. You're too trusting.
Not everybody in the world is so nice, you know.
Thank you. I'll be careful.

Glad to hear it. Oh, and keep what I told you between us,
you hear? I can't have you telling Mai or Nakai-san.
Huh? Oh, all right...
Looking forward to going up against you again. See you!

(Wow, T-Set's Azusa-san rescued me. I think she must be a
good person at heart.)
Well, thank you for everything! I'll be seeing you.
You bet. Thanks for stopping by. See you!

(Phew. That does it for making the rounds. I'd better get
back to the agency.)

(Oh, that's that comedian who's famous for reading palms,
Shuhei Shimada-san.)

(I can't believe it's actually him! They say his readings
are scarily accurate. I've always wanted to have him read my
palm one day.)
Huh? Isn't that that girl?

It is! You're Haruka-chan, aren't you? From the Princess
League?

Yes, that's right! I'm Haruka Sawamura. It's very nice to
meet you!

That's a good, strong greeting! I like it! I'm Shuhei
Shimada. I've been watching you on TV.
Oh, thank you! I see you on TV all the time, too!
